cemc-gauss7-1999-02.title: Test each choice
cemc-gauss7-1999-02.body:
- Digit sum $2+8+7 = 17$ is not a multiple of $3$, so not divisible by $3$ (or $6$).
- $287$ is odd, so not divisible by $4$.
- It doesn't end in $0$ or $5$, so not divisible by $5$.
- $287 = 7 \times 41$. ✓

**Answer: (D) 7**

cemc-gauss7-1999-03.title: Two bags per kilogram
cemc-gauss7-1999-03.body:
Each kilogram fills $2$ bags, so $35.5$ kg fills $35.5 \times 2 = 71$ bags.

**Answer: (E) 71**

cemc-gauss7-1999-04.title: Missing piece
cemc-gauss7-1999-04.body:
Each term fills half of what is left to reach $2$: after adding all four, we are $\frac18$ short of $2$, so the sum is $2 - \frac18 = \frac{15}{8}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{15}{8}$**

cemc-gauss7-1999-05.title: Odd and even rules
cemc-gauss7-1999-05.body:
- $6^2 = 36$ (even)
- $23 - 17 = 6$ (odd minus odd is even)
- $9 \times 24$ is even (24 is even)
- $96 \div 8 = 12$ (even)
- $9 \times 41 = 369$: odd times odd is odd.

**Answer: (E) $9\times41$**

cemc-gauss7-1999-06.title: Angle sum
cemc-gauss7-1999-06.body:
The angles of a triangle add to $180°$, so the other two add to $180° - 72° = 108°$.

**Answer: (C) 108**

cemc-gauss7-1999-09.title: Trace the route
cemc-gauss7-1999-09.body:
Following the paths, André can go $A \to B \to C \to \dots \to J$ in order. From $J$, the only ways to reach $K$ pass through $G$ again or retrace a path, which is not allowed. So he visits $A$ through $J$: $10$ sites.

**Answer: (D) 10**

cemc-gauss7-1999-10.title: Split into squares
cemc-gauss7-1999-10.body:
The marked segments are all $3$ cm, so the shape can be cut into $4$ identical $3 \times 3$ squares (one on top, three along the bottom). The area is $4 \times 9 = 36\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: (B) 36**

cemc-gauss7-1999-11.title: All minus the inside
cemc-gauss7-1999-11.body:
There are $10 \times 5 = 50$ tiles. The tiles not touching a wall form an $8 \times 3$ rectangle of $24$ tiles. So $50 - 24 = 26$ tiles touch a wall.

**Answer: (A) 26**

cemc-gauss7-1999-11.title: Count the border
cemc-gauss7-1999-11.body:
The two long walls have $10$ tiles each, and the two short walls have $5 - 2 = 3$ more each (the corners are already counted): $10 + 10 + 3 + 3 = 26$.

**Answer: (A) 26**

cemc-gauss7-1999-12.title: Every fifth number
cemc-gauss7-1999-12.body:
With five people, each one's numbers go down by $5$. Henry says $34, 29, 24, \dots, 9, 4$. Then Iggy says $3$, Joan $2$ and Fred $1$.

**Answer: (A) Fred**

cemc-gauss7-1999-12.title: Remainders
cemc-gauss7-1999-12.body:
Henry says the numbers that leave remainder $4$ when divided by $5$ (34, 29, ...). Going around: Iggy gets remainder $3$, Joan $2$, Fred $1$, Gail $0$. Since $1$ leaves remainder $1$, Fred says it.

**Answer: (A) Fred**

cemc-gauss7-1999-13.title: Count
cemc-gauss7-1999-13.body:
The grid is $5 \times 5 = 25$ small squares and $9$ of them are shaded. $\frac{9}{25} = \frac{36}{100} = 36\%$.

**Answer: (C) 36**

cemc-gauss7-1999-14.title: Check the conditions
cemc-gauss7-1999-14.body:
$12^2 = 144$ and $13^2 = 169$, so the number is between $144$ and $169$: this leaves $147, 156, 165$. $156$ is even; $147$ has no digit $5$. $165$ is odd, has a $5$, and $1+6+5 = 12$ is a multiple of $3$.

**Answer: (D) 165**

cemc-gauss7-1999-15.title: Green out of total
cemc-gauss7-1999-15.body:
There are $36 + 18 + 9 + 6 + 3 = 72$ cubes, $9$ of them green. Probability $= \frac{9}{72} = \frac18$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac18$**

cemc-gauss7-1999-16.title: Compute speeds
cemc-gauss7-1999-16.body:
Speed $=$ distance $\div$ time:

| | distance (km) | time (min) | speed (km/min) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alison | 1 | 20 | 0.05 |
| Bina | 1 | 50 | 0.02 |
| Curtis | 3 | 30 | 0.1 |
| Daniel | 5 | 50 | 0.1 |
| Emily | 5 | 20 | 0.25 |

Emily is fastest.

**Answer: (E) Emily**

cemc-gauss7-1999-16.title: Read the graph
cemc-gauss7-1999-16.body:
Fast means far in little time: a point far to the right and low down. Emily's point (5 km in 20 min) goes the greatest distance (tied with Daniel) in the least time (tied with Alison), so she beats everyone.

**Answer: (E) Emily**

cemc-gauss7-1999-17.title: Find the second term
cemc-gauss7-1999-17.body:
The second term is $9 - 2 = 7$. Then the sequence is $2, 7, 9, 16, 25, 41, 66, 107$. The eighth term is $107$.

**Answer: (C) 107**

cemc-gauss7-1999-19.title: Subtract the white triangles
cemc-gauss7-1999-19.body:
The rectangle is $14 \times 4 = 56\text{ m}^2$. The two unshaded triangles each have base $7$ m (the marks show the bottom is cut in half) and height $4$ m, so together they cover $2 \times \frac12 \times 7 \times 4 = 28\text{ m}^2$. The shaded part is $56 - 28 = 28\text{ m}^2$.

**Answer: (B) 28**

cemc-gauss7-1999-19.title: Half of each half
cemc-gauss7-1999-19.body:
Cut the rectangle down the middle into two $7 \times 4$ rectangles. In each one, the white triangle has the full base and height of that half, so it is exactly half of it. So the shaded part is half of the whole: $\frac12 \times 56 = 28\text{ m}^2$.

**Answer: (B) 28**

cemc-gauss7-1999-20.title: Find the magic sum
cemc-gauss7-1999-20.body:
$1 + 3 + 5 + \dots + 17 = 81$, so each of the three rows sums to $81 \div 3 = 27$.

- Right column: $B + 13 + 3 = 27$, so $B = 11$.
- Top row: $A + 1 + 11 = 27$, so $A = 15$.
- Left column: $15 + 5 + D = 27$, so $D = 7$.
- Bottom row: $7 + E + 3 = 27$, so $E = 17$.

$A + E = 15 + 17 = 32$.

**Answer: (A) 32**

cemc-gauss7-1999-21.title: Find routes, then look backwards from T
cemc-gauss7-1999-21.body:
The board has 5 columns and 4 rows.

- From $S$: 3 right, 2 up lands on $R$. From $S$: 3 up, 2 right lands on $P$.
- From $P$: 3 down, 2 right lands on $W$. From $W$: 3 left, 2 up lands on $Q$.

To land on $T$ (row 3, column 3), the move before must start 3 squares away in one direction and 2 in the other. Going 3 squares up or down from row 3 leaves the 4-row board, and going 3 squares left or right from column 3 leaves the 5-column board. So no move ends at $T$.

**Answer: (D) $T$**

cemc-gauss7-1999-22.title: Try the possible bases
cemc-gauss7-1999-22.body:
The base length and width add to $9$: $8 \times 1$, $7 \times 2$, $6 \times 3$ or $5 \times 4$, with areas $8, 14, 18, 20$. The height is $42 \div \text{area}$, which must be a whole number, so only $7 \times 2$ works: height $42 \div 14 = 3$.

**Answer: (D) 3**

cemc-gauss7-1999-22.title: Factor 42
cemc-gauss7-1999-22.body:
$42 = 2 \times 3 \times 7$. The block's dimensions multiply to $42$, and two of them add to $9$. The factorizations are $1\times1\times42$, $1\times2\times21$, $1\times3\times14$, $1\times6\times7$, $2\times3\times7$; only $2 + 7 = 9$ works, so the height is $3$.

**Answer: (D) 3**

cemc-gauss7-1999-23.title: Angles around M
cemc-gauss7-1999-23.body:
Around point $M$: $\angle PMQ = 360° - 90° - 60° - 60° = 150°$ (the square's angle and the two equilateral triangles' angles). Also $MP = MJ$ and $MQ = ML$, and $MJ = ML$ (sides of the square), so triangle $PMQ$ is isosceles with $MP = MQ$. Its base angles are $\frac{180° - 150°}{2} = 15°$.

**Answer: (B) 15**

cemc-gauss7-1999-24.title: Use the cheapest marbles
cemc-gauss7-1999-24.body:
Each small marble scores at least $1$, each medium at least $3$, each large at least $5$. To use many marbles, use all $10$ small ones (at least $10$ points), leaving at most $13$ points for the others. Each further marble costs at least $3$, so at most $4$ more: $10 + 4 = 14$ marbles.

$14$ is possible: $10$ small through hole 1 ($10$ points), three medium through hole 3 ($9$) and one medium through hole 4 ($4$): $10 + 9 + 4 = 23$.

$15$ marbles would score at least $10 + 5 \times 3 = 25 > 23$.

**Answer: (C) 14**

cemc-gauss7-1999-25.title: Count points per game
cemc-gauss7-1999-25.body:
Four teams make $6$ pairs, each playing $4$ times: $24$ games. A game with a winner gives out $3$ points; a tie gives out $1 + 1 = 2$ points, one less. With no ties there would be $24 \times 3 = 72$ points; the actual total is $22 + 19 + 14 + 12 = 67$. Each tie accounts for one missing point, so there were $72 - 67 = 5$ ties.

**Answer: (C) 5**

cemc-gauss7-1999-25.title: Equations
cemc-gauss7-1999-25.body:
Let $w$ games have a winner and $t$ be ties. Then $w + t = 24$ and $3w + 2t = 67$. Subtracting twice the first: $w = 67 - 48 = 19$, so $t = 5$.

**Answer: (C) 5**
